findings.title: 3.7's full-suite gate cannot pass: `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` still drives the old `createContextPipeline` signature until 4.1
findings.description: Task 3.7 requires `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm -r test` to all pass before committing the seam removal. But `core/tests/adoption/adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` is only deleted in 4.1. At 3.7 it still exists, still calls `createContextPipeline(dir, { adoptionStateWrites: stateWrites, squadronProbe: fakeProbe })` (line 68) against the new one-argument signature — a `tsc --noEmit` error in core's test project — and still asserts the removed rendering and state writes (`FACTS_HEADING = '### Adoption Facts'` at line 24, `readAdoptionState(root)).toBe('in_progress')` at lines 123/209). So the workspace is red at the point the task file says to commit, and a junior AI has no instructed option other than deleting/ad-hoc editing 4.1's file early or committing a failing suite. Fix: move the deletion of `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` into Section 3 (before 3.7), or split 3.7's commit so the typecheck/test gate runs after 4.1.

findings.title: 3.2a's intermediate commit gate is false: 3.1–3.2 break assertions in `pipeline-integration.test.ts` that are not removed until 3.3
findings.description: 3.2a is stated as a working, tested checkpoint ("**Success:** `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test` pass"). It cannot be. The `brownfield build with an injected squadron probe` block (lines ~129–195) builds through the real pipeline and asserts exactly the two renderings that 3.1 and 3.2 delete: `Comprehension: ${COMPREHENSION}` at line 184, the probe JSON/`WARNING` facts at ~165, and the unavailable-probe statement at ~176. Those cases are only deleted by 3.3 (`the probeReturning block`), i.e. after the commit. Either pull the pipeline-integration brownfield/probe deletions into 3.1–3.2 (they are render assertions, so they belong with the render removal), or drop `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test` from 3.2a and gate that commit on the two touched suites plus a note that pipeline-integration is knowingly red until 3.3.

findings.title: 5.1's self-mutation check adds an edit-and-revert cycle no success criterion requires
findings.description: The design's D5 asks for the purity assertions (snapshot unchanged, concept prompt present, no `### Adoption Facts`, no `sq` marker, CLI/MCP parity, explicit-key check) — all present. The extra step "temporarily add a `writeFileSync` of `.context-forge.toml` … confirm the snapshot assertion fails, then revert" is a test-sensitivity check beyond the criteria, and it costs a source edit/revert round-trip inside a 3-effort task that already carries the checkout builder, the fake-`sq` PATH shim, the snapshot helper, four runs and two one-off checks. Reasonable to keep as a NOTE, but if the section needs trimming this is the first candidate; splitting the harness from the run matrix would also make 5.1 independently completable.

findings.title: Post-deletion the `sq` marker assertion can only guard against reintroduction, not against live spawning
findings.description: 5.1 runs after 4.4 deletes `runSquadronProbe`, so nothing on the build path can execute `sq` and the marker check is structurally unsatisfiable. It is a legitimate regression guard and matches D5's wording ("a fake `sq` executable placed first on `PATH`"), and the PATH hygiene the design's Special Considerations require (test-process-only `PATH`, restore in `afterAll`) is spelled out correctly. Noted only so the reviewer does not read the marker as proof of behavior that the deletions already guarantee.

findings.title: `**Commit**:` marker style is inconsistent across sections
findings.description: 2.3 and 3.2a put the commit on the task heading as a plain line, while 4.1–4.4, 3.7 and 5.1 make it a `- [ ] Commit: …` sub-checkbox. The substantive rule is met — markers sit at working, tested points, not after every task and not only at the end, and 6.3's conditional commit is correctly phrased as "otherwise nothing to commit" — so this is a formatting nit for the checker agent, not a coverage problem.

findings.title: Criterion-to-task traceability and design references check out against the code
findings.description: The design's Migration Plan and Tests lists are fully accounted for: `adoption/contracts.ts` trimmed to `AdoptionError` (4.2 — justified, since the kept `comprehensionAnalysis.ts:33/50`, `planningArtifacts.ts:45`, `sourceVolume.ts:47/90` and `adoptionState.ts:19` all still throw it), `adoptionState.ts` write-vs-read split (4.3), `adoption-completed` removal (4.3, with the exhaustive-switch check named as the compiler gate), probe + contract test + fixture deletion (4.4, matching `detection/index.ts:8-17`), `ContextToolOptions`/`adoptionStateWrites` removal from `generateContext` and `registerContextPipeline` (3.6, matching `contextTools.ts:11/65/100/152`), `integrationSetup.ts` probe option (3.6), `node.ts` comment (4.2), and the `outOfTreeLinks.test.ts` rewrite onto kept functions (4.1). 6.2's named exception is accurate — `COMPREHENSION_PROFILE_VARIABLE = 'fileComprehension'` does live at `detection/comprehensionAnalysis.ts:15` — and the 6.1 guide-warning criteria name tests that exist at `cli/tests/commands/build.test.ts:91` and `mcp-server/tests/contextTools.test.ts:162`. The build-tooling claims are also correct: root `package.json` has `lint`/`typecheck` and no format script, and core builds to `dist/` that `cli`/`mcp-server` typecheck against, which is why 3.4's `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core build` step is placed where it is. No merge or push task appears, per the git rules.
